title: Concise outage snapshot with action choices (draft)
body:
TL;DR:

Short update we can post to the status page and email customers. Minimal language, three actionable choices for customers, and simple integrity attestation so customers can decide whether to ask for replay/evidence. Intended for a broad customer audience (engineering leads + product owners).

What happened (one sentence):
Between 2029-12-22 03:14–04:05 UTC a routing logic regression caused a subset of production requests (approx. 0.6% of tokens) to be routed to a downgraded model variant with stale KV cache snapshots, producing higher-latency and occasionally truncated structured outputs.

Impact (concise bullets):
- Affected tenants: ~120 (high-traffic tenants disproportionately represented).
- Visible symptoms: elevated latencies, intermittent truncated JSON/structured output, and occasional duplicate chunks in streaming responses.
- Duration: first detection 03:14 UTC; controlled rollback to stable routing at 03:48 UTC; late replays/cleanup through 04:05 UTC.
- Customer-visible window (status page): 03:14–04:05 UTC.

Our immediate mitigation:
- Automatic rollback of routing policy at 03:48 UTC to stable model variants.
- Temporarily increased cache TTL for warm prefixes to reduce further KV-mismatch replays.
- Disabled new deploys to affected routing code path while we investigate.

Why this matters for customers:
- Some responses during the interval may be incomplete or show higher latency than normal. For deterministic workloads (e.g., structured output/JSON parsing, embeddings), you may observe inconsistencies compared with later requests.

Customer choices (pick one):
1) No action — treat as transient. We confirm request integrity (hashes) below; if you do nothing, no further action required.
2) Request replay of affected request set for reconciliation (self-serve or with CS help). Replays will re-run requests against the stable variant, and we provide a diff/evidence package. There may be rate limits; expect turnaround 24–72 hours depending on request volume.
3) Opt into a bulk re-evaluation (for spec-driven pipelines). We can run a regression re-evaluation using your saved prompt sets and produce a report showing token-level differences and quality deltas. This is a paid-support offering for larger workloads; we’ll provide a scoped proposal on request.

Integrity attestation (what we can guarantee right now):
- Request ingest logs are intact. We have end-to-end request hashes (client request -> internal request id -> stored output hash). These were not tampered with.
- For the affected interval we observed KV cache divergence; outputs generated during that window may differ from canonical outputs produced after rollback.
- We can supply per-request evidence: original request payload, execution trace id, server-side output, and canonical re-run output. Evidence package includes hashes and timestamps.

How to request evidence/replay (steps):
1) Open a CS ticket referencing JIRA-INC-9876 or reply to this message with the tenant id + timeframe (default: 2029-12-22 03:14–04:05 UTC).
2) Indicate whether you want: a) per-request replay + diffs (free, SLAs apply), b) bulk re-eval report (paid option for large prompt sets).
3) We will confirm scope, expected ETA, and any rate limiting.

Suggested short status page update (one-line + details):
- One-line: "Degraded routing caused intermittent higher latency and truncated outputs for a subset of requests — mitigated and rolled back; partial replays available on request."
- Details block (for status page): "Timeline: 03:14 UTC detection; 03:48 UTC policy rollback; 04:05 UTC controlled cleanup. Impact: ~0.6% token surface area, intermittent truncated structured outputs. Action: Customers can request replays or evidence via support with tenant id and timeframe. Engineering note: routing/regression under active investigation; no data exfiltration detected."

Draft email to affected customers (short):
Subject: Brief update: transient routing regression on 2029-12-22 (actions available)
Hi <CustomerName>,
We detected a transient routing regression on 2029-12-22 that affected a small percentage of requests. We rolled back the change within ~34 minutes and have begun cleanup. If you saw truncated outputs or higher latency, you can request a replay/evidence package. Reply to this email or open a ticket referencing JIRA-INC-9876 and include the tenant id and timeframe; we will prioritize high-severity/production-impact customers.
Thanks,
Aisha (Customer Success)

FAQ (anticipated customer questions):
Q: Was customer data exposed?
A: No evidence of data exfiltration. Logs show requests stayed within expected clusters and internal memos indicate no external access.

Q: Will this change model behavior for subsequent requests?
A: No — rollback restored routing to the pre-change variant and cache warming reverted to normal. Any differences are constrained to the affected window.

Q: How long to get a replay?
A: For up to 10k requests we aim for 24–48 hours. Larger volumes 48–72 hours or we will provide a scoped plan.

Ops checklist (notes to self / engineering):
- Confirm final RCA (root cause) ticket link and add to customer artifact list.
- Prepare automated per-tenant evidence package generator (PR #4521 partially implements).
- Validate that cache TTL tweak has no regressions (SRE follow-up).
- Decide whether to publish a postmortem with timeline + technical appendix (recommended).

Unresolved items (we should not surface to customers yet):
- Whether the regression originated from a canary rollout config or a feature flag race (investigation ongoing).
- Exact list of affected tenant ids (security will confirm sharing rules).

Attachments we can provide to customers on request:
- Per-request payload + server output + canonical re-run output (zipped, with hashes).
- Short timeline (machine-readable CSV) showing request ids and timestamps.
- Concise engineering summary (non-sensitive).

Tone guidance for posting: keep public status updates factual, not speculative. Offer options (do nothing, ask for replay, request scoped re-eval). Avoid deep technical root cause until RCA is complete.

Notes to CS on prioritization: prioritize tenants who: a) flag production regressions, b) have high request volume during window, c) have compliance/regulatory requirements.

---
Draft end.

Quick links for internal use: Confluence incident doc: CONFLUENCE-INCIDENT-2029-12-22 (link above); RCA placeholder: JIRA-INC-9876; Evidence generator PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4521.

Comments: please review phrasing for status page (Maya) and confirm attachment packaging (Luca).
